files_summary.wikipedia.json: Wikipedia article store keyed by exact title; each article has summary, sections (named-heading -> text), links (titles of related included articles), and key_facts.
files_summary.README.md: Schema, lifecycles and business rules of this benchmark's datastore.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_search_wikipedia
tool_schemas.description: Searches Wikipedia for articles that match the provided query string and returns a list of matching article titles (up to the requested limit). It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, or with a non-integer or invalid limit. It may also refuse limits that are not positive or are unreasonably large for a single request.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_get_article
tool_schemas.description: Retrieves the full article content for the given Wikipedia page title and returns the page text and associated metadata available from Wikipedia. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title. It also refuses titles that do not resolve to an article (for example, nonexistent pages or ambiguous titles that cannot be resolved).

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_get_summary
tool_schemas.description: Returns a concise encyclopedia-style summary for the specified Wikipedia page title. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title. It also refuses titles that do not resolve to an article, such as nonexistent pages or titles that cannot be uniquely resolved.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_summarize_article_for_query
tool_schemas.description: Generates a summary of the specified article tailored to the provided query focus and returns the query-focused summary text (constrained by max_length). It refuses requests missing title or query, or where either is empty. It also refuses invalid max_length values (non-integer, non-positive, or too large) and titles that do not resolve to an article.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_summarize_article_section
tool_schemas.description: Summarizes a specific section within the given article and returns a section-focused summary limited by max_length. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title or section_title. It also refuses requests where the article does not exist, the section cannot be found in that article, or max_length is not a valid positive integer.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_extract_key_facts
tool_schemas.description: Extracts a requested number of key facts from the specified article, optionally scoped to a topic within the article, and returns those facts as structured items. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title, or where the title does not resolve to an article. It also refuses invalid count values (non-integer, non-positive, or too large) and may refuse a topic_within_article that cannot be matched to any relevant content in the page.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_get_related_topics
tool_schemas.description: Returns a list of topics related to the specified article, derived from the page’s links and categories, up to the requested limit. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title, or where the title does not resolve to an article. It also refuses invalid limit values (non-integer, non-positive, or too large).

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_get_sections
tool_schemas.description: Lists the section headings for the specified Wikipedia article and returns them in document order. It refuses requests with a missing or empty title. It also refuses titles that do not resolve to an article, including nonexistent pages or titles that cannot be uniquely resolved.

tool_schemas.name: wikipedia_get_links
tool_schemas.description: Returns the set of links contained within the specified Wikipedia article (as link targets/titles available from the page). It refuses requests with a missing or empty title. It also refuses titles that do not resolve to an article, and may refuse pages where links cannot be retrieved due to missing or restricted content.

metadata.name: Lexipedia Insight Service
metadata.description: A backend service that searches Wikipedia articles and returns full text, summaries, sections, related topics, links, and extracted key facts for downstream applications.
